angles.drive: You save before you spend, every time. Something put away lets you relax, so you save a little from every month rather than enjoy all of one. Spend one saved month on something you want, and you learn what the saving was for.
angles.cost_self: Saving first is how you stay calm. You put money away ahead of anything you would enjoy, because the account quiets your worry. Spend some on yourself every so often, and you stop paying for safety with the years you save for.
angles.cost_others: Saving first hands your people the careful version of you. You put the savings ahead of the trip together, and give them caution instead of company. Spend one saved thing on them a year, and you hand them the part of you the saving protects.

angles.drive: You sleep on a decision before you make it, even a small one. Waiting a night costs nothing and hurrying costs plenty, so you would rather lose a day than a deal. Sleep on the big ones, and decide the small ones before bed.
angles.cost_self: Sleeping on a choice keeps your money safe, and it keeps you late. You wait a night ahead of saying yes, since being wrong costs more. Say yes the same day once a season, and you stop losing chances to whoever answered first.
angles.cost_others: Whenever you sleep on an answer, you leave someone waiting overnight. You would rather be sure tomorrow than quick today, and you hand the wait to whoever asked. Give the small answers before bed, and you keep the patience of the people around you.

angles.drive: You show up every day the same way, noticed or not. Being counted on matters more to you than being exciting, so you show up on dull days too. Show up for yourself once a week as well, since steady love needs a steady supply.
angles.cost_self: Showing up daily is your way of staying sure of someone. You keep the routine ahead of your rest, since a missed day feels like a crack. Miss one on purpose now and again, and you get the rest showing up runs on.
angles.cost_others: What you give the ones you love is that you keep showing up. You hand them presence rather than surprise, and you let them know each day's shape in advance. Change the shape once a month, and you add something to look forward to.

angles.drive: You hold money back long after holding it back makes sense. Having it in the pool feels safer than having it out, so you hold it rather than use it. Remember that money held back is only safe until the day it is needed.
angles.cost_self: Holding back keeps the floor from dropping. You hold money ahead of using it even on things you need, because spending feels like losing. It is worth remembering that held money buys nothing, and what you go without is what it was for.
angles.cost_others: Whenever someone close asks, you hold back first and help second. Keeping the pool whole comes ahead of the ask, and you hand them a yes with most of it held back. You already know that the smaller yes is what stays with them.

angles.drive: You count the cost before you let yourself want anything. Knowing the price makes a thing safe, so you count what a dinner costs ahead of what it is worth. Bear in mind that the count is right and the dinner was the point.
angles.cost_self: Being caught short is the thing counting every cost protects you from. You would rather know what a kindness costs than take it, and you count the free ones too. Notice that counting has a price too, paid in closeness you never let in.
angles.cost_others: Counting every cost reaches the people you love. You keep a running total of what each of them costs rather than brings, and you let it show in what you give back. Keep the other column too, since the one you read from shows.

angles.drive: You wait for the sure thing, and it rarely comes on time. Being certain means more to you than being early, so you wait past the moment for yes. You know by now that waiting is a decision too, with its own price.
angles.cost_self: Waiting too long keeps you from being wrong. You want the sure yes more than the early one, and you wait until the choice makes itself. Do not forget that the price of waiting is the deals and people that stopped waiting for you.
angles.cost_others: When someone needs your answer, you wait until you are sure. You put being certain ahead of being there, and you leave whoever asked holding a question. Know that a late yes reaches most people as a no, whatever you meant by it.

angles.drive: You handle resources the way careful water handles a landscape, never taking more than the channel can hold. The purchase gets slept on, the debt gets declined, the plan keeps a margin. Boring, people say, until their own accounts get interesting in the bad way.
angles.cost_self: The car was chosen after the insurance quote, the reliability data, and one conversation with a mechanic you trust. It has now outlasted three of your friends’ flashier choices, at half the total cost. The spreadsheet that picked it is still on your laptop, mildly famous.
angles.cost_others: Friends consult you before their big decisions the way travelers check the depth of a river before driving in. Your questions are unexciting and save fortunes: what does it cost per year, what happens if it breaks. Several disasters in your circle simply never happened. That was you.

angles.drive: Your resources move like a reliable stream, in on schedule, out with intention, never flash-flooding. The salary lands, the transfers fire, the obligations get met a little early. Drama has no purchase on your finances, and the calm compounds as quietly as the interest.
angles.cost_self: Rent has arrived on the first for eleven consecutive years, across three landlords, one recession, and a broken leg. The current landlord once called to check the transfer was real, so rare is the species. You are the tenant reference other applicants wish existed.
angles.cost_others: The people downstream of you, family, dependents, one perpetually struggling friend, plan their lives around a reliability they have stopped noticing. The support just arrives, monthly, like weather in a fortunate climate. Nobody asks what maintaining a stream that steady requires. It requires everything, daily.

angles.drive: The future finds you already provisioned. The renewal date is in the calendar, the emergency fund holds six months, the umbrella lives in the car. Your readiness is so habitual it looks like luck: things simply never seem to catch you without the relevant item.
angles.cost_self: When the layoffs came, your household absorbed the news with a strange calm: the fund was there, the resume was current, the numbers had been run in advance during a peaceful January. The panic that visited every other affected house found yours already interviewed and hired.
angles.cost_others: People tease the preparations right up until they need them, at which point you become briefly, intensely popular. The jump cables, the spare charger, the printed copy: someone borrows one weekly. You have become the reason other people can afford to be spontaneous. Nobody sends a card.

angles.drive: Your resources pool behind walls you keep raising. The money accumulates and does not move, the generosity is rationed through a narrow spillway, and downstream, things that needed watering are visibly dry. The reservoir is impressive. Reservoirs, unvisited, are just deep places holding still.
angles.cost_self: The account crossed the threshold you once named as enough, and the threshold moved the same week, upward, as it always moves. Your niece’s tuition request took three weeks to answer and came back a loan, papered, at interest. Family dinners since have had a different acoustics.
angles.cost_others: People stopped asking, which you registered as peace. The requests dried up, the little fundraisers route around you, and the reputation settled like silt: comfortable, careful, closed. The wealth is real and growing. What it is for remains, to everyone including you, the open question.

angles.drive: Every offer arrives at your door pre-suspected. The deal has a catch, the kindness has an angle, the stranger has a reason: your default read is downstream contamination, and proof of purity is a standard almost nothing meets. You are rarely cheated. You are also rarely surprised by joy.
angles.cost_self: The neighbor’s offer to water your plants during your trip triggered a full risk assessment: motive, key custody, precedent. You declined with thanks and paid a service. The plants did fine. The neighbor waved differently afterward, from slightly further away, permanently.
angles.cost_others: People approach you with their cards face up and their movements slow, having learned that anything else reads as an angle. The honest ones find the screening mildly insulting and mostly stop volunteering. What gets through your filter is genuinely safe. So little gets through.

angles.drive: Letting go, of money, of objects, of the way Sunday is supposed to run, activates something in your grip that logic cannot pry open. The sunk cost stays sunk and held, the worn-out thing stays shelved, and your hands, at any given moment, are completely full.
angles.cost_self: The vacation fund has existed for nine years and never once been spent, each proposed trip failing the final review at the moment of booking. The money is for vacations. The vacations are somehow never quite worth the money. The fund grows, a monument to trips unrisked.
angles.cost_others: Prying anything from you, a concession, an old coat for the charity bag, an admission that plans changed, has a known difficulty rating among your people. They mostly stopped trying and started working around the grip. Your hands hold everything. Notably, lately, that includes very little of theirs.
